module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 826

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/826](https://www.erdosproblems.com/826)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos826

/--
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$
$$
  \tau(n + k) \ll k?
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_826 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), { n | ∀ k ≥ 1, σ 0 (n + k) ≤ C * k }.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos826

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, “Problems”, Math. Balkanica 4 (1974), 203–204, problem 4.33.2(II), p. 203, included in https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, Erdos826.erdos_826. The outer existential correctly supplies one uniform positive constant for infinitely many n and every k ≥ 1. Mathlib’s σ 0 is the divisor-counting function, the inequality is over ℝ, and n+k is always positive. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiled successfully, evaluated small divisor counts, checked boundary cases, and proved equivalence with the positive-n formulation. The source still records problem 826 as open; Lau’s reported bound involving k^C is weaker and does not warrant changing the status.
